Unattributed, unrefuted for 38 years, while its neighbours 596/598/599/601 all carry explicit disproofs. Counterexample: the **Hoffman–Singleton graph** (n=50). Diameter 2 ⇒ every vertex sees 43 others at even distance ⇒ LHS = 43. RHS = χ + χ(Ḡ) = 4 + 25 = **29**. Margin **+14** — and the whole certificate is just one explicit 4-colouring plus one explicit perfect matching, checkable by hand. Plus an unbounded family (blow-ups C₅[t], every t ≥ 8, margin ≈ n/10) and a razor-thin 26-vertex witness with margin exactly **1/13**. Zero violations over all 1,246,251 connected triangle-free graphs on ≤12 vertices. Verifier: 144,542 assertions, exit 0, pure Python — commit `775591b`, README §7i.

It claimed: if 4·m(Ḡ) ≤ freq[max # of K₄'s at a vertex], then G is *well total dominated* (every minimal total dominating set is minimum). Counterexample: **C₅ ∨ K₈** on 13 vertices (complement = C₅ + 8 isolated vertices). m(Ḡ)=2 and the 8 universal vertices each lie in 175 K₄'s vs 112 for the cycle vertices, so freq = 8 and the hypothesis holds *with equality* 8 ≤ 8 — yet γ_t = 2 while {0,1,3} is a minimal total dominating set of size 3. It's true for every connected graph of order ≤ 9 (exhaustively checked), and the family C₅ ∨ K_t breaks it for every n ≥ 13. Verifier + writeup landing in graffiti-verification shortly.

Shearer, October 1988) — "−2nd smallest eigenvalue ≤ the matching number" for connected graphs — is FALSE. Open 37 years 10 months, and it survived the 1990–91 Los Alamos Cray sweep because every connected graph on ≤9 vertices satisfies it. Minimum order is exactly **ten**: exactly 2 of the 11,716,571 connected graphs on 10 vertices refute it (one in 5.9 million), both book graphs; exactly 4 of the 1,006,700,565 on 11 vertices (one in 252 million). The margin is unbounded — B(k, k(k−1), k(k−1)) has matching number 2 and spectrum {k+1, k−1, 0…, −k, −k}. Restricted to trees it first fails at n=12, unique witness the double broom D(5,4).
